thesis: COLM has already re-rated after the Oct 29 earnings gap and now sits extended (RSI 68.5, about 7% above SMA20) and above the mean analyst target, with no fresh catalyst. The earnings jump is margin-driven on roughly 2% revenue growth, and forward P/E is above trailing P/E, so consensus prices in no further growth. Nov 19 reversed from a 77.36 intraday high to a 74.30 close, which marks supply at the 52-week high. Meanwhile the regime is risk-off (QQQ below 50/200-day, VIX at the 99.5th percentile), and a high-beta discretionary apparel name that rallied 25% in 21 days is exposed to a liquidation or squeeze unwind. Short interest near 19% of float cuts both ways, and a reversal would be sharp. A director is selling into the strength.
